summary.intent: Evaluate how well the Wisp plugins served front-end work and design ideation across the techworx/orin-dx and pages projects by mining ~810 session transcripts, then act on the findings, including testing the hypothesis that plugin workflows are too rigid for exploratory work.
summary.outcome: Four parallel investigations found the plugins strong for behavioral specs and cross-spec consistency but poorly suited to visual and ideation work, supporting the rigidity hypothesis. The session then updated Callisto, Caliper, Monokl and Pages to enable the current plugins, and fixed 34 docs and Codex-parity audit findings plus an escalation off-by-one on the wisp branch, with `just check` passing. A ceremony-removal batch was proposed but not started.

repo: Corpus sizes were misread at first: the orin-dx project dir holds only 2 real sessions and the pages dir about 7. The remaining ~140 and ~590 files are subagent transcripts. Plugin work is concentrated in orin-dx b8d16e96 and pages 24655582.
Plugin agents appeared in very few top-level sessions. All design ideation ran through Artifacts, forks, general-purpose agents and local dev servers with Playwright screenshots, not plugins.

No plugin has a browser, screenshot, visual or generative mode. spec@1 has no fields for tokens, layout, breakpoints or visual intent, and the workspace-manifest capability enum is closed, so a spec can pass muse's gate while saying nothing about appearance.
Muse docs reference a ranger accessibility hazard taxonomy that never existed, so implemented a11y is never checked.

The gates caught real behavioral defects before code: contrast ratios recomputed from tokens, cross-spec contradictions, and plan ordering and stale breakpoint bugs. They did not catch visual defects such as a non-fullscreen NavSheet or touch-target growth, which the user found by eye.
Gate loops were often wording churn on 110-120 criterion specs. The 3-retry escalation was ignored by the orchestrator, and 60-130KB spec and plan files stalled agents.

orin-dx-site is not a git repo and holds only brand/ artifacts. All specs, plans and reviews live in ~/projects/pages/docs. Pages has 538 commits, many carrying Claude-Session and Entire-Checkpoint trailers.
On 14 Oct the user declared an exploratory mode: lean less on specs and tests, and add them once ideas narrow. SPEC-014/015/016 were never gated.
Tests encoded wrong values, such as a 760px boundary pinned in code and tests. The 13 Oct pruning deleted 34% of tests, including CSS tests, and a11y and visual checks were rebuilt only on 16 Oct.
ADR 015 sets two rounds for gates, but the hook, sentinel README, diagrams, transcript-metrics and docs still carried the old 3-retry cap in several places. `just check` did not catch these.

Codex harness gaps that `just check` missed: round rules only in judge.md, gate-readiness.md, evidence.md and constitution.md not shipped to the plugins that load them, and bare skill names in the Codex guide skills.
Claude-only enforcement (validate-handback.py for exit-gate verdict@3 only, route-guard.py in six plugins) was undocumented outside the guide README.
Repo conventions conflict across projects: Callisto forbids session links in commits, Caliper requires them, and the changeset formats differ in all three repos.

code.finding: ROUTES covers only the 5 exit-gate agents. navigator:challenger emits `overall` rather than verdict@3, so its retry cap is prompt-only. The hook was updated to reject an un-escalated second-round fail.
over_retry_cap hardcoded `count > 3`, the old cap. It now uses RETRY_CAP = 1, and the test was changed to retry_count 2 so it distinguishes the two caps.
The description was 528 characters, over the 450 cap. test_skill_routing only covered 4 plugins, so it went unnoticed. The test now covers all plugins.

Now generates marketplace descriptions in both marketplace.json files from each plugin.json, and `--check` verifies them. After any plugin.json or Codex edit, re-run `just claude-manifests-sync` and `just marketplace-sync`.

workflow: Run mechanical scans first (skill and agent counts per session) to size a large transcript corpus, then delegate qualitative analysis to parallel subagents and forward the user's hypothesis to them mid-run.
Verify corpus assumptions before reporting. File counts included subagent transcripts, so the initial session numbers were wrong.
Separate observed fact from inference in subagent reports, and treat hand-backs as unverified model output.
Keep the property and drop the ritual. Red-green order is gone (ADR 008), and what remains is a test that discriminates.
Visual decisions need rendered evidence. The user repeatedly asked for pictures instead of prose descriptions of what they were approving.
Run `just check` in addition to targeted audits, because many docs and parity inconsistencies pass it.
Split parallel audit fixes by file ownership, run full checks and re-sync manifests before committing. A concurrent edit made one first check fail on a stale generated manifest.
Run commit and push as separate commands. In Monokl a refused commit ran alongside the trail command, and the branch was published empty.

friction: The initial session count was wrong because subagent transcripts were counted as sessions.
Subagent and teammate reports were repeatedly truncated mid-report and had to be re-requested via SendMessage.
In Monokl, a commit was refused while `entire trail create` ran and published the branch empty. It was fixed with a follow-up commit and push.
The orin-dx pr-bot token cannot be minted from this machine, so PRs for wisp-plugins, callisto and monokl were blocked.
Concurrent agent edits to shared files caused a stale generated manifest to fail the first `just check`, and one of my edits did not apply because the docs auditor had already changed the line.
The orchestrator in the transcripts ignored the gate's escalation rule, and large specs and plans stalled agents.
open_items: Decide whether to add the ceremony-removal batch to the branch: remove navigator:estimator, change AGENTS.md's 'Red-to-Green' label, relax the 'no TBD before planning' gate, drop commit-per-task from plans, and single-source versions.
Measure before making the `reasoning` field optional or ablating persona backstories (runbook paired runs).

Design a sketch/explore mode for early work, with a divergent generation mode, a spike skill without gates, a promote path to spec, browser/screenshot capability kinds, and visual-intent fields in specs.

Resolve the cross-repo conflicts: session links in commits, changeset format, who opens PRs, Caliper's hard-coded rustup path, Pages' `rtk` prefix rule, the orin-dx-site git status, and where brand/ is the source of truth.
Fix remaining audit gaps: Codex manifest categories, role cards shipped to every plugin including guide, route-guard docs for Codex, and the ADR 015 wording on the navigator challenger hook coverage.

Not checked by the audits: Antigravity behavior, whether the SubagentHandback hook matcher works on a live host, `claude plugin validate`, symlink installs, plugin CHANGELOGs, and parity for several mason, vanguard and weaver skills.
Open the blocked PRs once the pr-bot token problem is solved.
